The 'best AI model' no longer exists. There are only the best models for specific tasks — and the pricing floor just collapsed.

54 new AI models have shipped in the last 90 days. That is roughly one every four days. This week alone: ByteDance launched UniVR-34B-Planning, Nvidia shipped nvDock and CWIP-1.0, and Mistral released Leanstral-1.5-119B — a 119-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model activating only 6 billion. Meanwhile, xAI's Grok 4.5 reset API pricing at $2/$6 per million tokens, and competitors matched within days.

For CTOs, the implication is structural: locking into a single model provider is now a liability, not a strategy. The performance gap between frontier models has compressed to the point where architecture — how you route tasks, evaluate outputs, and swap providers — matters more than which model you picked last quarter.

For CEOs, the strategic read is clear: AI compute costs are deflating rapidly. The companies that build modular, multi-model orchestration layers now will capture that deflation as margin. The ones running monolithic integrations will keep paying yesterday's prices for yesterday's capabilities.

This is not a technology trend. It is a procurement and architecture discipline.
